title: RISC-V Based Secure Processor Architecture for Return Address Protection
problem: RISC-V embedded systems vulnerable to buffer overflow attacks, particularly stack-based attacks that alter program control flow. Memory-based attacks are significant challenge for RISC-V security.
motivation: RISC-V foundation working on zicfiss (backward edge CFI) and zicfiip (forward edge CFI) extensions. Hardware-based return address protection requires low-overhead architecture changes.
method: Hardware-based approach leveraging existing Return Address Stack (RAS) with minimal microarchitecture changes and limited software overhead. Protects against buffer overflow attacks targeting control flow. Tested with buffer-intensive benchmarks and RIPE benchmark.
key_novelty: Low-overhead RISC-V hardware return address protection using RAS with minimal area/timing overhead; protects against BFO and Spectre RAS-related attacks.
contributions: RISC-V hardware return address protection mechanism
limitations: Abstract only; specific overhead measurements on typical benchmarks not detailed; limited to Rocket Core validation; Spectre protection claims not quantified; RISC-V extension integration not fully detailed.
primary_theme: Hardware-based control flow integrity for RISC-V
